newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium courts Toyota - Prime Minister.
newsitem.headline: Belgium courts Toyota - Prime Minister.

text.p: Belgium's Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene said on Sunday he hoped Japanese car maker Toyota would locate its second, planned European car assembly plant in the country following a final decision by Renault of France to pull out.

Renault confirmed on Saturday plans announced in February to shut its Vilvoorde assembly plant near Brussels this year. In a change from its original plan, Renault said, however, it would save 400 out of 3,000 jobs at the site by maintaining an unspecified form of industrial activity.
Dehaene told VTM news Belgium was now actively lobbying Toyota about its plans to build a new small car factory in Europe by the turn of the century.
Toyota has said little about the plan, except it will decide on a location before the end of 1998.
Dehaene said, however, Toyota had ruled out taking over the Vilvoorde factory, which is squeezed between a railway line, canal and Brussels' motorway ring road.
Toyota said earlier this month it would double the size of its European parts centre at Diest, central Belgium, at a cost of around $24 million. Toyota Motor Europe is also based in Brussels.
